legis-36.title: The Constitution (Thirty-sixth Amendment) Act, 1975, with the Statement of Objects and Reasons
legis-36.publisher: Government of India, Ministry of Law and Justice, Legislative Department
legis-36.note: Read from the web.archive.org snapshot of 27 February 2023. The Statement of Objects and Reasons records the Sikkim Assembly's resolution of 10 April 1975 abolishing the institution of the Chogyal, and the special opinion poll of 14 April 1975 (59,637 for, 1,496 against, electorate about 97,000). The Act is dated 16 May 1975 and is deemed in force from the day the Council of States passed the Bill; its article 371F deems the Assembly formed by the elections of April 1974, with thirty-two members, the Legislative Assembly of the State of Sikkim.

sikkim-code.title: The Sikkim Code, Volume I: Sikkim Acts (1975-1982)
sikkim-code.note: Read from the web.archive.org snapshot of 3 June 2024 of the Digital Himalaya copy. The Foreword dates Sikkim's incorporation as a State of India from 26 April 1975 under the Constitution (Thirty-sixth Amendment) Act, 1975; the Sikkim Panchayat Act, 1982 (section 116) repeals the Sikkim Panchayat Act, 1965 and its Block Panchayats; the Sikkim Bazar Committees Act, 1969 is still cited.

jpi-1975-1.title: Journal of Parliamentary Information, Vol. XXI, No. 1 (January-March 1975): G. R. Rajagopaul, The New Constitution of Sikkim: An Analysis; Parliamentary and Constitutional Developments
jpi-1975-1.note: The Internet Archive's copy of the Lok Sabha Digital Library item eparlib.sansad.in/handle/123456789/764118 (the library itself refused this session). The article by the Constitutional Adviser to the Government of Sikkim describes the Agreement of 8 May 1973, the elections of April 1974 held with the help of the Election Commissioner of India, the Assembly's resolution of 11 May 1974, and the Government of Sikkim Act, 1974 (Assembly elected every four years, s. 11; an Election Commission appointed by the Chogyal on the Government of India's nomination, s. 8; electors aged 20, s. 10).

jpi-1975-3.title: Journal of Parliamentary Information, Vol. XXI, No. 3 (July-September 1975): Parliamentary and Constitutional Developments; Sessional Reviews
jpi-1975-3.note: The Internet Archive's copy of the Lok Sabha Digital Library item eparlib.sansad.in/handle/123456789/761998. Records the Constitution (Thirty-fifth Amendment) Act in force from 1 March 1975 (associate status, one member each in the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha to be elected), the Chief Magistrate's order of 29 March 1975 restraining the Assembly from electing them, the Assembly's resolution of 10 April 1975, the referendum of 14 April 1975 (59,637 for, 1,496 against), the Lok Sabha's passage of the statehood Bill on 23 April and the Rajya Sabha's on 26 April 1975, and the President's assent on 16 May 1975.

lsd-1974-09-04.title: Lok Sabha Debates, 4 September 1974: Constitution (Thirty-sixth Amendment) Bill
lsd-1974-09-04.note: The Internet Archive's copy of the Lok Sabha Digital Library item for 4 September 1974. The Minister of External Affairs states that elections were held in Sikkim in April 1974, for the first time on the basis of one man, one vote; a member records that the National Party won one seat and the Sikkim Congress the others.

lsd-1973-04-09.title: Lok Sabha Debates, 9 April 1973: Statement re Situation in Sikkim
lsd-1973-04-09.note: The Internet Archive's copy of the Lok Sabha Digital Library item for 9 April 1973. The Minister of State for External Affairs reports charges of rigging against the Sikkim Darbar after the recent general elections, and the Government of India's taking over Sikkim's administration at the Chogyal's request of 8 April 1973.

grover-1974.title: Sikkim and India: Storm and Consolidation
grover-1974.note: Published in New Delhi in 1974; chapter III dates each Sikkim Council election from the Darbar's proclamations and press reports (March to May 1953, November 1958, an interim election in 1960, March 1967, April 1970, January-February 1973) with seat numbers and party results, and chapter VIII covers the Assembly election of April 1974 (32 seats, conducted under the supervision of the Election Commission of India in three stages; the Assembly inaugurated on 10 May 1974). Appendix reproduces the India-Sikkim Treaty signed at Gangtok on 5 December 1950.

basnet-1974.title: Sikkim: A Short Political History
basnet-1974.note: Published by S. Chand and Co., New Delhi, 1974 (listed in the Lok Sabha Secretariat's Journal of Parliamentary Information, October-December 1974). Records the Indo-Sikkim Treaty of 5 December 1950 and the village panchayat elections of December 1950, boycotted by the Sikkim National Party.

classes.name: Sikkim Council
classes.locator: https://archive.org/details/dli.pahar.3456 (chapter III: First Elections to Sikkim Council 1953; Second Elections, November 1958; Third Election, March 1967; Sikkim's Fourth Election 1970; Sikkim's fifth Election, January-February 1973)
classes.note: The advisory legislature set up by the Maharaja's State Council and Executive Council Proclamation of 1953, sitting for three years unless dissolved. In 1953 it had 17 members, 12 elected (six Bhutia-Lepcha and six Nepali seats) and 5 nominated by the Maharaja; the Proclamation of 16 March 1958 raised it to 20, with 14 elected (six Bhutia-Lepcha, six Nepali, one Sangha seat chosen by an electoral college of the lamas of the recognized monasteries, and one general seat for the whole country) and 6 nominated, and a candidate needed 15 per cent of the other community's votes to be returned; from 1967 it had 24 members, 18 elected (seven Bhutia-Lepcha, seven Nepali, the Sangha seat, and general, Scheduled Caste, and Tsong seats in the general constituency) and 6 nominated. An election tribunal unseated five members in 1959 and an interim election followed in 1960. The Darbar ran and declared every election; the 1973 count, begun on 29 January, was boycotted by the Sikkim National Congress and the Sikkim Janta Congress, and the agitation that followed led to the Agreement of 8 May 1973 and the Assembly elected in April 1974.
classes.finest_note: Constituency (communal seats within territorial constituencies, the general constituency, and the Sangha electoral college); no official return is online.
classes.disposition_reason: Results were declared by the Sikkim Darbar and printed in its gazette; the Government of Sikkim's Old Durbar Gazette search (sikkim.gov.in) returns no record for any year from 1950 to 1975, the Sikkim Palace Archives copy at the British Library (EAP880) answers only with a bot challenge, and the Sikkim Legislative Assembly's site refused this session.

dates.quote: The elections for the first Sikkim Council were held from March to May 1953. About 40 per cent of the electorate of 60670 went to the polls.
dates.note: Twelve elected seats (six Bhutia-Lepcha, six Nepali) and five nominated; the Sikkim National Party won all the Bhutia-Lepcha seats and the Sikkim State Congress all the Nepali seats. Dates from Grover (1974), not yet confirmed from the Darbar's own record.

dates.quote: Elections were again held for the second time in Sikkim in November 1958.
dates.note: Fourteen elected seats of twenty under the Proclamation of 16 March 1958; the Sikkim State Congress took 8, including one Bhutia-Lepcha seat and the general seat. Due in 1956, the Council's term having been extended by proclamation.

dates.quote: On account of these vacancies an interim election was held in 1960.
dates.note: Interim election for the five seats whose members an election tribunal unseated in 1959, followed by a by-election in Namchi in December 1960 that returned Nidup Bhotia (Sikkim National Party) under the communal counting rule although Kazi Lhendup Dorji polled more votes.

dates.quote: Sikkim went to the polls for the third time in its history in March 1967.
dates.note: Eighteen elected seats of twenty-four; the Sikkim National Congress won 8, the Sikkim National Party 5, and the Sikkim State Congress 2, with the Tsong, Sangha, and Scheduled Caste seats held by members of no party. The Council elected in 1958 was dissolved on 1 May 1962 and no election was held until 1967.

dates.quote: went to polls fourth time in April, 1970.
dates.note: Seventy-two candidates for eighteen seats; the Sikkim National Party won 7, the Sikkim National Congress 5 (including the general seat), the Sikkim State Congress 4, and independents 2.

dates.quote: After the general elections in Sikkim recently, the tension had aggravated as there were charges of malpractices, corruption and rigging up of elections of the part of Sikkim Darbar.
dates.note: Polling in January 1973, with counting from 29 January (Grover 1974, who dates the election January-February 1973); 55 candidates for eighteen seats; the Sikkim National Party won 11, the Sikkim National Congress 5, and the Sikkim Janta Congress 2. The opposition boycotted the count, and the Government of India took over the administration on 8 April 1973.

classes.name: Sikkim Assembly
classes.name_en: Sikkim Assembly, general election of April 1974
classes.locator: https://archive.org/details/eparlib.nic.in.764118 (pages 6-8: In pursuance of the Agreement, elections were held in Sikkim in April 1974 with the help of the Election Commissioner of India; The Sikkim Assembly: elections every four years, s. 11)
classes.note: Created by the Agreement of 8 May 1973 between the Chogyal, the political parties, and the Government of India, which called for elections on adult suffrage and one man, one vote, with seats balanced so that no community dominated; the Bhutia-Lepcha and Nepali communities had equal representation. The 32 members were elected in April 1974, polling in three stages under the supervision of the Election Commission of India; the Sikkim Congress won all but one seat (Lok Sabha, 4 September 1974; Grover gives 29 of 32) and the Sikkim National Party one. The Assembly was inaugurated on 10 May 1974, passed the Government of Sikkim Bill on 28 June 1974 (promulgated on 4 July 1974: elections every four years, an Election Commission appointed by the Chogyal on the Government of India's nomination), resolved on 10 April 1975 to abolish the Chogyal, and became the Legislative Assembly of the State of Sikkim on 26 April 1975 under article 371F of the Constitution of India. No by-election is recorded before that date.
classes.finest_note: Constituency; no official return is online.
classes.disposition_reason: The constituency results were declared by the Chief Election Officer of Sikkim, working with the Election Commission of India, and printed by the Government of Sikkim; neither the Old Durbar Gazette search on sikkim.gov.in (no record for 1974), the Sikkim Legislative Assembly's site (refused this session), nor the Election Commission of India (connection reset; its statistical reports for Sikkim begin with 1979) holds them online. The Lok Sabha records give only the seat total and the party split.

dates.quote: In pursuance of the Agreement, elections were held in Sikkim in April 1974 with the help of the Election Commissioner of India
dates.note: Thirty-two seats (article 371F(b)(i) of the Constitution of India, Legislative Department); polling in three stages in April 1974 (Grover 1974). The Sikkim National Party won one seat and the Sikkim Congress the rest (Lok Sabha Debates, 4 September 1974).

classes.name: Special opinion poll
classes.name_en: Special opinion poll on the Assembly's resolution abolishing the Chogyal (referendum of 14 April 1975)
classes.note: The only popular vote on a question in the Kingdom: the Sikkim Assembly resolved on 10 April 1975 that the institution of the Chogyal be abolished and Sikkim become a constituent unit of India, and submitted the resolution to the people. The Government of Sikkim held the poll throughout Sikkim on 14 April 1975 and the Chief Minister communicated the result to the Government of India on 15 April. The Lok Sabha Secretariat calls it a referendum.
classes.finest_note: National totals of votes for and against, and the approximate electorate, from the Government of India's Statement of Objects and Reasons; no result by polling station or constituency is online.

dates.note: Approval of the Assembly's resolution of 10 April 1975; the Lok Sabha Secretariat gives the same figures (Journal of Parliamentary Information, July-September 1975).

classes.name: Panchayat
classes.locator: https://archive.org/details/dli.pahar.3457 (page 97: Panchayat elections were held in December, 1950. These elections were boycotted by the National Party)
classes.note: Elected village panchayats, announced as a first step towards popular government, were first elected in December 1950, when the Sikkim National Party's boycott left only a handful functioning. The Sikkim Panchayat Act, 1965 set up panchayats again, at the village level from 1966, with Block Panchayats whose assets passed to the State under the Sikkim Panchayat Act, 1982 (Sikkim Code, Volume I). Gangtok had no elected municipality before the Gangtok Municipal Corporation Act, 1975; bazaars were run by Bazar Committees under the Sikkim Bazar Committees Act, 1969, whose manner of constitution is not recorded in the sources reached.
classes.finest_note: Village panchayat; no official return is online.
classes.disposition_reason: No date, seat count, or result of any panchayat election from 1950 to 1975 is in an official source reached here: the Sikkim Darbar's gazette is not online (the Old Durbar Gazette search on sikkim.gov.in returns no record for those years), and the text of the Sikkim Panchayat Act, 1965 was not found.

dates.quote: Panchayat elections were held in December, 1950.
dates.note: Boycotted by the Sikkim National Party; only a handful of panchayats could function (Grover 1974).

dates.quote: At the village level Panchayats have been established since 1966.
dates.note: Panchayats under the Sikkim Panchayat Act, 1965; whether and when they were elected is not dated in a source reached here.

classes.name: Chogyal
classes.locator: https://legislative.gov.in/constitution-thirty-sixth-amendment-act-1975 (The institution of the Chogyal is hereby abolished)
classes.disposition_reason: A hereditary monarchy (Sir Tashi Namgyal, then his son Palden Thondup Namgyal); the institution was abolished by the Assembly's resolution of 10 April 1975, approved in the poll of 14 April 1975. The Dewan (to 1973), the Chief Executive (from 1973), and the Executive Councillors and Ministers were appointed, the last on the Chief Executive's advice from among the elected members (Government of Sikkim Act, 1974, ss. 25 and 28).

classes.name: Representatives of Sikkim in Parliament
classes.name_en: Members for Sikkim in the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha, to be elected by the Sikkim Assembly (associate status, 1975)
classes.locator: https://archive.org/details/eparlib.nic.in.761998 (page 421: Under the Act, two Members were to be elected—one each for Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha; on March 29 the Chief Magistrate restrained the Sikkim Assembly from electing them)
classes.disposition_reason: Not a popular vote: under the Constitution (Thirty-fifth Amendment) Act, in force from 1 March 1975, the Sikkim Assembly was to elect one member to each House of the Indian Parliament; the Chief Magistrate of Sikkim restrained it on 29 March 1975, and no such election is recorded before Sikkim became a State on 26 April 1975.
